contract.pre_condition: vaddr is page-aligned by type and denotes an eligible user virtual page in vmem: it lies within the valid user range and is not a protected, kernel, or shared mapping that this operation lacks authority to remove. vmem's page-table representation, abstract mapping relation, cleanup metadata, and ownership capabilities are coherent. Any required relation among self, vmem, and the active address space holds. The body itself validates none of these conditions and relies on contracts for Vmem::unmap and UserFrame destruction.
contract.post_condition: On Ok(true), Vmem::unmap returned Ok(Some(frame)), and this body consumed and dropped frame before returning. Subject to the callee and destructor contracts, the selected abstract mapping is absent, all unrelated mappings and preserved identities are unchanged, and authority for the removed backing user frame is released or transferred exactly once. On Ok(false), Vmem::unmap returned Ok(None); subject to its contract, the abstract mapping relation is unchanged. Cleanup may alter hidden page-table representation only when reclamation preconditions hold and without changing the abstract mapping result.
contract.failure_condition: If Vmem::unmap returns Err(e), this body returns Err(e), does not report successful removal, and performs no subsequent explicit mutation or frame release. The body alone does not establish failure atomicity: Vmem::unmap may have partially changed page-table representation, cleanup state, mappings, or ownership before returning Err. Its failure contract must either preserve all observable abstract state or precisely characterize permitted partial mutation while forbidding an unreported removed mapping, unrelated mapping changes, or lost or duplicated frame authority.

abstraction.name: Selected-user-page mapping with representation, ownership, and cleanup separation
abstraction.abstract_state: The state is a tuple (M, R, A, C, I). M maps each eligible user virtual page to either no mapping or a backing user-frame identity with abstract permissions. R contains page-directory and lower-level page-table objects, entries, flags, links, and allocation metadata. A records ownership and allocator authority for mapped frames, returned UserFrame values, and free frames. C records lower-level table occupancy, cleanup eligibility, ownership, pending reclamation, and reclaimed status. I records active address-space identity, vmem identity, allocator identity, and protected, kernel, and shared mapping identities.
abstraction.projection: project(R) = M for eligible user mappings. A present eligible leaf entry for virtual page v projects to M[v] equal to its frame identity and abstract permissions; an absent leaf projects to no mapping. Empty intermediate tables and their allocation or reclamation do not independently contribute mappings.
abstraction.preserved_state: For selected page v, every M[u] with u different from v is preserved. Active address-space identity, vmem identity, allocator identity, protected, kernel, and shared mappings, and authority unrelated to the selected mapping are preserved. Reclamation may alter R and C only for an empty lower-level table that is validly owned and reclaimable, and must preserve project(R) except for removal of M[v] when that mapping existed.
abstraction.hidden_representation: Page-table allocation layout, directory and table indices, empty-but-allocated lower-level tables, entry encoding, TLB maintenance mechanism, cleanup ordering, and concrete allocator bookkeeping are hidden if their future observable behavior refines M, A, C, and I.
abstraction.observation_boundary: The operation is observed after the complete Rust call expression, including Vmem::unmap, Option::is_some, destruction of any returned UserFrame, and construction of Result<bool, Error>. Observable effects are the returned result, future address translation and Vmem observations of the abstract mapping relation, preserved identities and mappings, and allocator-visible authority or later frame reuse. Intermediate page-table states are outside the boundary only if they cannot be observed through concurrency, faults, panics, callbacks, reentrancy, or missing synchronization.

obligations.title: Result-to-mapping correspondence
obligations.claim: For eligible v, Vmem::unmap(v) returns Ok(Some(f)) if and only if the pre-state M maps v to f, and then the post-state mapping is exactly the pre-state mapping with v removed. It returns Ok(None) if and only if v was absent, and then the mapping relation is unchanged.

reintegration.rationale: The child analysis does not prove the required result-to-mapping correspondence. It presents that correspondence only as an intended contract and explicitly leaves unknown whether try_find_user_frame exactly reflects logical mapping presence, whether successful leaf and hardware removal changes exactly the selected abstract mapping, and whether empty-table cleanup preserves all other mappings. These are open child obligations, not established evidence.
reintegration.caller_effect: The child supports only the weaker claim that Ok(None) follows when try_find_user_frame returns None and that Ok(Some(f)) can follow after finding f, matching the selected leaf to f, successfully removing that leaf, invoking hardware unmapping, and completing required cleanup. It does not support the parent claim that Ok(Some(f)) occurs if and only if the pre-state mapping maps v to f, that the post-state is exactly the pre-state mapping with v removed, or that Ok(None) occurs if and only if v was abstractly absent and leaves the mapping relation unchanged.
reintegration.remaining_gap: Prove child O1 and O2 to connect try_find_user_frame results to abstract mapping presence and establish lookup purity; O3 and O4 to connect the unique selected leaf mutation to the logical mapping; O5 to show cleanup preserves the projection; O6 to establish exact hardware-translation removal and framing; and O7 to show relevant valid-state errors and panics are unreachable. Only then can the bidirectional parent correspondence close.

contract.pre_condition: Caller-usable intended contract for VirtMemoryManager::try_unmap_upage: the manager denotes a live address-space identity A; vaddr is page-aligned; and the world satisfies the common coherent-representation/readiness invariant connecting A's logical user-page mappings, page metadata, backing-owner accounting, software page tables, hardware translations, and cleanup structures. For the valid-page case, all internal lookups, conversions, leaf removal, hardware mirroring, and empty-table cleanup operations must be provably non-failing. The weaker body-local contract requires only the typed alignment and the conditions individually required by operations reached along the executed path; it consequently permits internal errors and partial mutation.
contract.post_condition: Under the intended total contract, if vaddr is outside A's valid user range, the function returns the designated invalid-range error (represented by BadAddress in the supplied implementation) and leaves the entire observed world unchanged. If vaddr is valid but has no mapping in A, it returns Ok(None) and preserves the world. If vaddr maps in A to logical page view P = (backing identity B, permissions and page metadata), it returns Ok(Some(owner-for-B)), removes exactly A's mapping and metadata for vaddr, removes exactly the corresponding software and hardware translation, and preserves every other mapping. B's contents remain unchanged. B remains in the logical backing store while any mapping in any address space or any detached retained owner exists; otherwise the returned value or associated ownership transition must account for the final ownership and reclamation protocol. Physical allocator/resource conservation is a separate postcondition and follows only from explicit ownership and allocator contracts. The supplied body locally justifies less: on Ok(Some(UserFrame::new(f))) it found f, checked the selected leaf against f, successfully unmapped that leaf, invoked hardware unmapping, and completed any required empty-table cleanup before returning; it does not by itself establish logical backing identity, permissions, last-owner behavior, allocator conservation, or the absence of internal failures under the intended readiness invariant.
contract.failure_condition: An address outside user space returns BadAddress before body-visible mutation and is intended to be an unchanged-state invalid-range failure. Under the intended coherent-representation/readiness precondition for a valid user page, other Err results and both panic sites are contract violations and must be proved unreachable rather than exposed as ordinary outcomes. Body-locally, errors can still arise from frame search, address construction, directory or table lookup, leaf lookup or removal, and directory cleanup. Failure atomicity is not established: in particular, pgdir.unmap may syntactically return Err after the leaf mapping, hardware translation, and user_page_tables entry have been removed. A lookup mismatch panics through unreachable!, and inconsistent table membership panics through expect.

abstraction.name: Lifecycle-scoped user-page mappings with shared backing ownership
abstraction.abstract_state: The world contains: (1) for each live address-space identity A, a partial map U_A from valid user virtual pages to logical page views containing backing identity B, permissions, and page metadata; (2) a backing store S mapping each live B to its contents and logical ownership state, including mappings across all address spaces and detached retained owners; (3) physical allocator/resource authority R, observed separately from logical mapping equality; (4) hidden software and hardware page-table representations and cleanup metadata; and (5) lifecycle state identifying which address spaces are live and which manager instance denotes A.
abstraction.projection: For a live manager denoting A, U_A(v) = (B, permissions, metadata) exactly when the authoritative logical metadata and coherent page-table representation identify the same mapping at v. The raw FrameAddress used by the supplied implementation is a representation-level locator for B, not the complete logical page view. Software leaf entries, hardware translations, try_find_user_frame results, page-directory entries, and user_page_tables membership must agree with this projection under the readiness invariant. Backing-store membership is projected from global mapped-owner and retained-owner state, not merely from whether A still maps B.
abstraction.preserved_state: A successful mapped-page removal preserves U_A at every page other than vaddr; all mappings and metadata in every other address space; the removed backing's contents; unrelated backings and ownership counts; unrelated software and hardware translations; lifecycle identities; and unrelated allocator authority. Removing A's mapping changes only the ownership contribution associated with that mapping. The backing remains logically live if another mapped or retained owner exists. Any last-owner transition and physical reclamation must follow separate ownership and allocator rules. Ok(None) and invalid-range failure preserve all components of the observed world under the intended contract. These frame properties require callee and representation contracts beyond the supplied body.
abstraction.hidden_representation: Raw frame addresses; pgdir entries; user_page_tables ordering and membership; PageTable leaf entries and nmapped counters; hardware page-table entries; address-wrapper conversions; metadata searched by try_find_user_frame; backing-owner counters or registries; detached-owner representation; allocator free lists; and generation or lifecycle tokens are hidden unless they affect a caller-visible mapping, ownership, resource, error, panic, or translation observation.
abstraction.observation_boundary: The caller-facing boundary includes the Result<Option<UserFrame>, Error>, the logical mapping U_A and page metadata, backing identity and contents, global mapped and retained ownership sufficient to determine backing-store liveness, software/hardware translation behavior, address-space lifecycle identity, and physical allocator/resource authority as a distinct world-level observation. Logical mapping equality alone does not imply allocator equality or conservation. Internal table layout, vector order, counters, and empty-table allocation remain hidden when they cannot affect those observations.

candidate_variants.semantic_difference: For a live address space satisfying coherent representation and readiness, a valid mapped page must return Ok(Some(owner-for-B)), a valid unmapped page must return Ok(None), and all internal lookup, removal, and cleanup errors and panics are unreachable. It specifies exact per-space mapping removal, shared-backing preservation or last-owner transition, hardware coherence, and separate resource conservation.

candidate_variants.name: Weaker body-local successful-result contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Claims only what follows after a returned result: BadAddress is mutation-free in the shown body; Ok(None) reflects try_find_user_frame returning None; and Ok(Some(f)) follows successful raw-leaf removal, hardware-unmap invocation, and completed cleanup. It permits internal Err outcomes, possible post-mutation partial states, and makes no independent claim about logical metadata, backing liveness, or allocator authority.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject a pgdir.unmap failure after removing the last leaf. This variant permits Err with partial mutation, while the intended total contract requires that failure to be unreachable in a ready state.

candidate_variants.name: Failure-atomic recovery contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Adds rollback or transactional behavior so every Err preserves logical mappings, backing ownership, software and hardware translations, and resource authority. This is stronger than both the intended ready-state contract and the supplied body's currently justified behavior.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Force any post-leaf-removal operation to fail and compare the complete pre- and post-world, including table membership and hardware translation.

candidate_variants.name: Logical-only unmap contract
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Observes per-space mappings, metadata, and backing contents but excludes allocator authority and possibly hardware translation from equality. It can declare two states equivalent despite different physical-resource ownership or translation behavior and is therefore insufficient for the requested world-level contract.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Compare two executions with identical U_A and backing contents but different allocator free lists, returned-frame authority, or hardware entries.

contract.pre_condition: vaddr is page-aligned by type and is a user-space address. For a total result-to-mapping correspondence contract, additionally require a representation invariant relating the abstract mapping M to try_find_user_frame and the selected PageTable entry, directory and table readiness, consistency of user_page_tables, and success of all fallible lookup, conversion, unmap, and directory-cleanup operations.
contract.post_condition: If the function returns Ok(None), try_find_user_frame(vaddr) returned None and the shown body performed no subsequent mutation; concluding that pre-state M lacked vaddr and that observable state is unchanged requires semantic and frame contracts for try_find_user_frame. If it returns Ok(Some(UserFrame::new(f))), try_find_user_frame selected frame address f, the selected PageTable lookup equaled f, PageTable::unmap succeeded, hw_unmap_user was invoked, and, when page_table.nmapped() reported zero, the corresponding user_page_tables entry was removed and pgdir.unmap succeeded. Concluding that post-state M is exactly pre-state M with vaddr removed requires the projection, leaf-unmap, cleanup, and hardware-mirroring obligations.
contract.failure_condition: A non-user address returns BadAddress before any body-visible mapping mutation. Other errors may arise from try_find_user_frame, address construction, directory or table lookup, PageTable lookup or unmap, and pgdir.unmap. The body does not establish failure atomicity: pgdir.unmap may return Err after the leaf PageTable entry, hardware mapping, and user_page_tables entry have already been removed. A lookup and frame mismatch panics through unreachable!, and a missing list entry during empty-table cleanup panics through expect.

abstraction.name: User virtual-page mapping projection
abstraction.abstract_state: M is a partial map from page-aligned user virtual addresses to FrameAddress values. If ownership is observable, the returned UserFrame is an ownership-bearing view of the removed frame rather than an additional mapping.
abstraction.projection: For each eligible virtual page v, M(v)=f exactly when the authoritative software page-table representation selected by v contains a present leaf entry mapping v to f. To justify this function's search and cleanup logic, try_find_user_frame, pgdir, user_page_tables, and the selected PageTable must agree with that authoritative projection.
abstraction.preserved_state: On successful removal, mappings for every virtual page other than vaddr, frame contents, and unrelated directory and table structures are preserved. On Ok(None), all abstract mappings and hardware-visible translations are preserved. These frame properties require callee contracts and are not established solely by the shown body.
abstraction.hidden_representation: pgdir entries, user_page_tables ordering and membership, PageTable leaf entries and nmapped counters, per-process hardware page-table entries, address-wrapper conversions, and metadata consulted by try_find_user_frame are hidden representation details.
abstraction.observation_boundary: The caller-facing observation boundary is the returned Result<Option<UserFrame>, Error> together with projected software mapping M immediately after return. If address translation or later memory access is observable, the boundary also includes the per-process hardware page table after hw_unmap_user. Internal vector order, empty table allocation, counters, and directory layout remain hidden except when they affect future operations, errors, panics, or translation.

implementation_assessment.claim: Ok(None) corresponds exactly to absence of vaddr in pre-state M and leaves M unchanged.
implementation_assessment.evidence: The only Ok(None) path is the None arm of try_find_user_frame(vaddr), and the shown body performs no subsequent operation on that path. The body does not establish that the callee's None means absence in M or that the callee is observationally read-only.

implementation_assessment.claim: Ok(Some(f)) identifies the frame mapped at vaddr before removal.
implementation_assessment.evidence: The returned frame address is obtained from try_find_user_frame, and the body checks that page_table.lookup(page_address) equals that address before unmapping. The semantic relation of both calls to pre-state M is unshown.

implementation_assessment.claim: On Ok(Some(f)), post-state M is exactly pre-state M with vaddr removed.
implementation_assessment.evidence: PageTable::unmap is called for PageAddress::new(vaddr), followed by hardware unmapping; empty-table cleanup occurs when nmapped()==0. The shown body does not prove the frame condition for other mappings, counter accuracy, hardware effect, or projection preservation during cleanup.

implementation_assessment.claim: For every eligible mapped vaddr, the function returns Ok(Some(f)).
implementation_assessment.evidence: Even after a frame is found, the code has explicit error paths for address conversion, directory lookup and readiness, page-table lookup, leaf unmap, and directory unmap. Therefore the claim does not follow unless eligibility excludes all such failures.

implementation_assessment.claim: The function is failure-atomic.
implementation_assessment.evidence: The code states that recovery after the hardware-unmap point would require remapping. In the empty-table path, pgdir.unmap can return Err after the leaf entry, hardware entry, and user_page_tables entry have been removed.

implementation_assessment.claim: The unreachable! and expect sites cannot panic under valid pre-state invariants.
implementation_assessment.evidence: Both sites rely on agreement among try_find_user_frame, the selected PageTable, pgdir, and user_page_tables. Those invariants are asserted informally but are not established by this body.

implementation_assessment.claim: A non-user vaddr returns BadAddress without changing the mapping representation.
implementation_assessment.evidence: The user-address check precedes all subsequent calls and mutations in the shown body, and its failing branch immediately returns Err.

obligations.title: Search-to-projection correspondence
obligations.claim: In a state satisfying the representation invariant, try_find_user_frame(v) returns Some(f) exactly when pre-state M(v)=f, returns None exactly when v is absent from M, and otherwise reports only specified representation or operational errors.
obligations.why_blocking: This gives semantic meaning to the Some and None branches; the body alone only branches on the callee's option tag.

suggested_callees.reason: Relate its option result to the authoritative mapping projection.

obligations.title: Search frame condition
obligations.claim: try_find_user_frame does not modify M, hardware translations, page-table membership, or other caller-observable state.
obligations.why_blocking: Without this frame condition, the early Ok(None) return does not imply that the mapping relation is unchanged.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish observational purity despite the mutable receiver.

obligations.title: Leaf unmap semantics
obligations.claim: Given a selected PageTable mapping page_address to f, successful PageTable::unmap(page_address) removes exactly that leaf mapping, preserves all other leaf mappings, and updates nmapped to the exact remaining mapping count; on error it has documented mutation behavior.
obligations.why_blocking: This is the central state-transition fact needed to derive post-state M as pre-state M without vaddr and to justify empty-table cleanup.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish exact removal, preservation, and error effects.
Establish that zero precisely characterizes an empty table.

obligations.title: Representation agreement invariant
obligations.claim: Whenever try_find_user_frame(v)=Some(f), the aligned directory entry is present, lookup_user_page_table selects the unique corresponding table in user_page_tables, and its lookup for v returns f; if that table becomes empty, its address is present exactly once in user_page_tables.
obligations.why_blocking: This excludes the reachable panic paths and connects search metadata, directory state, and the table actually mutated.

obligations.title: Empty-table cleanup preservation
obligations.claim: When the selected table has no remaining mappings, removing its user_page_tables entry and successfully calling pgdir.unmap removes only empty representation structure and preserves M for every other virtual page.
obligations.why_blocking: The successful Some path may delete an entire table representation, so preservation of unrelated mappings does not follow from leaf unmapping alone.

suggested_callees.reason: Specify directory-entry removal and preservation of unrelated mappings.

obligations.title: Hardware mirror correspondence
obligations.claim: hw_unmap_user(v) removes the hardware translation for exactly v, preserves translations for other pages, and agrees with the software projection after successful return.
obligations.why_blocking: If actual address translation is observable, software-only removal is insufficient for the caller-facing mapping contract.

suggested_callees.reason: Establish exact hardware unmapping and preservation of unrelated translations.

obligations.title: Error-state characterization
obligations.claim: For each fallible operation, characterize whether Err preserves the pre-state or may leave a partial unmap; in particular, determine the state after pgdir.unmap fails following leaf, hardware, and vector removal.
obligations.why_blocking: This determines whether eligibility can ensure total correspondence and whether callers may safely retry or continue after Err.

reintegration.rationale: The child analysis does not prove the required result-to-mapping correspondence. It presents that correspondence only as an intended contract and explicitly leaves unknown whether try_find_user_frame exactly reflects logical mapping presence, whether successful leaf and hardware removal changes exactly the selected abstract mapping, and whether empty-table cleanup preserves all other mappings. These are open child obligations, not established evidence.
reintegration.caller_effect: The child supports only the weaker claim that Ok(None) follows when try_find_user_frame returns None and that Ok(Some(f)) can follow after finding f, matching the selected leaf to f, successfully removing that leaf, invoking hardware unmapping, and completing required cleanup. It does not support the parent claim that Ok(Some(f)) occurs if and only if the pre-state mapping maps v to f, that the post-state is exactly the pre-state mapping with v removed, or that Ok(None) occurs if and only if v was abstractly absent and leaves the mapping relation unchanged.
reintegration.remaining_gap: Prove child O1 and O2 to connect try_find_user_frame results to abstract mapping presence and establish lookup purity; O3 and O4 to connect the unique selected leaf mutation to the logical mapping; O5 to show cleanup preserves the projection; O6 to establish exact hardware-translation removal and framing; and O7 to show relevant valid-state errors and panics are unreachable. Only then can the bidirectional parent correspondence close.
